aliases: read brain signal into a command
summary: The roadmap front door for the engine: turn brain signal into a decoded intent that can drive a build. Real, existing pieces already cover the whole chain: open EEG hardware, a unified streaming SDK, and ML that classifies the signal into an intent. That intent string then becomes the goal you hand to anything-engine, so thinking becomes the input to the search for how to build.

capabilities.query: eeg headset openbci muse brain signal
mne eeg intent classification machine learning

build_steps.title: Put on the headset and stream
build_steps.detail: Acquire raw EEG from an OpenBCI board (open hardware) or a Muse 2, and stream it with BrainFlow (one SDK across boards) or muse-lsl over Lab Streaming Layer.

build_steps.title: Decode an intent
build_steps.detail: Filter and window the signal (MNE), train a classifier (e.g. motor-imagery or SSVEP targets) to map brain states to a small vocabulary of intents. BrainPad is a worked example of the pipeline.

build_steps.title: Hand the intent to the engine
build_steps.detail: Map the decoded intent to a goal string and run it through anything-engine: `node cli.mjs "<decoded goal>"`. The search for how to build it runs itself. This is the loop the whole project points at: think it, and the components to build it assemble.

safety: Consumer EEG is non-invasive and low-risk, but it is sensitive personal biometric data. Keep raw brain data local and consented; never stream it to a third party by default. This is a research/maker pipeline, not a medical device.
